chapters.name: Solutions
keyPoints: Temperature Dependence: Mass %, ppm, mole fraction, and molality do not change with temperature; molarity and volume % change with temperature.

Henry's Law Constant ($K_H$): Higher $K_H$ at a given pressure indicates lower gas solubility. $K_H$ increases with temperature $\implies$ gases are more soluble in liquids at lower temperatures (aquatic life is more comfortable in cold water).

Ideal Solutions: Obey Raoult's law at all concentrations; $\Delta_{\text{mix}}H = 0$, $\Delta_{\text{mix}}V = 0$; A-B intermolecular forces $\approx$ A-A and B-B forces (e.g., n-hexane + n-heptane, benzene + toluene, bromoethane + chloroethane).

Non-Ideal Solutions with Positive Deviation: A-B interactions are weaker than A-A and B-B; $\Delta_{\text{mix}}H > 0$, $\Delta_{\text{mix}}V > 0$; $p_{\text{total}} > p_1^\circ x_1 + p_2^\circ x_2$; form minimum boiling azeotropes (e.g., ethanol + acetone, $\text{CS}_2$ + acetone, 95% ethanol + 5% water).

Non-Ideal Solutions with Negative Deviation: A-B interactions are stronger than A-A and B-B (often due to new H-bonding); $\Delta_{\text{mix}}H < 0$, $\Delta_{\text{mix}}V < 0$; $p_{\text{total}} < p_1^\circ x_1 + p_2^\circ x_2$; form maximum boiling azeotropes (e.g., phenol + aniline, chloroform + acetone, 68% $\text{HNO}_3$ + 32% water).

Reverse Osmosis: Occurs when an external pressure greater than the osmotic pressure ($\Pi$) is applied on the solution side; pure solvent passes through the semipermeable membrane (SPM: cellulose acetate) from solution to solvent side.

formulas.name: Mass Percentage (w/w)
formulas.latex: \text{Mass } \% = \frac{w_B}{w_A + w_B} \times 100 \qquad w_B = \text{mass of solute}, w_A = \text{mass of solvent}

formulas.name: Volume Percentage (V/V)
formulas.latex: \text{Volume } \% = \frac{V_B}{V_{\text{total}}} \times 100 \qquad V_B = \text{volume of solute}, V_{\text{total}} = \text{solution volume}

formulas.name: Parts Per Million (ppm)
formulas.latex: \text{ppm} = \frac{w_B}{w_{\text{solution}}} \times 10^6 \qquad \text{Used for trace quantities}

formulas.name: Mole Fraction (x)
formulas.latex: x_A = \frac{n_A}{n_A + n_B},\; x_B = \frac{n_B}{n_A + n_B} \qquad x_A + x_B = 1; \text{ dimensionless}

formulas.name: Molarity (M)
formulas.latex: M = \frac{n_B}{V\text{ (in L)}} = \frac{w_B \times 1000}{M_B \times V\text{ (in mL)}} \qquad \text{Unit: mol L}^{-1}; \text{ temperature-dependent}

formulas.name: Molality (m)
formulas.latex: m = \frac{n_B}{w_A\text{ (in kg)}} = \frac{w_B \times 1000}{M_B \times w_A\text{ (in g)}} \qquad \text{Unit: mol kg}^{-1}; \text{ temperature-independent}

formulas.name: Henry’s Law
formulas.latex: p = K_H x \qquad p = \text{partial pressure}, K_H = \text{Henry's constant}

formulas.name: Raoult’s Law (Volatile)
formulas.latex: p_1 = p_1^\circ x_1,\; p_2 = p_2^\circ x_2 \qquad p_{\text{total}} = p_1 + p_2 = p_1^\circ + (p_2^\circ - p_1^\circ)x_2 \qquad p_i^\circ = \text{vapour pressure of pure component } i

formulas.name: Vapour Phase Composition
formulas.latex: y_1 = \frac{p_1}{p_{\text{total}}},\; y_2 = \frac{p_2}{p_{\text{total}}} \qquad y_i = \text{mole fraction in vapour phase (Dalton's Law)}

formulas.name: Relative Lowering of Vapour Pressure
formulas.latex: \frac{p_1^\circ - p}{p_1^\circ} = i x_2 \approx i \frac{n_2}{n_1} = i \frac{w_2 M_1}{M_2 w_1} \qquad \text{Dilute solution of non-volatile solute in volatile solvent}

formulas.name: Elevation of Boiling Point
formulas.latex: \Delta T_b = T_b - T_b^\circ = i K_b m = i \frac{1000 K_b w_2}{M_2 w_1} \qquad K_b = \frac{R M_1 T_b^{\circ 2}}{1000 \Delta_{\text{vap}}H} \text{ (Ebullioscopic constant)}

formulas.name: Depression of Freezing Point
formulas.latex: \Delta T_f = T_f^\circ - T_f = i K_f m = i \frac{1000 K_f w_2}{M_2 w_1} \qquad K_f = \frac{R M_1 T_f^{\circ 2}}{1000 \Delta_{\text{fus}}H} \text{ (Cryoscopic constant)}

formulas.name: Osmotic Pressure
formulas.latex: \Pi = i C R T = i \left(\frac{n_2}{V}\right) R T = i \frac{w_2 R T}{M_2 V} \qquad C = \text{molarity}, R = 0.0831\text{ L bar K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}

formulas.name: Van ’t Hoff Factor (i)
formulas.latex: i = \frac{\text{Observed Colligative Property}}{\text{Calculated Colligative Property}} = \frac{M_{\text{normal}}}{M_{\text{abnormal}}} \qquad i = \frac{\text{Total moles after dissociation/association}}{\text{Moles before dissociation/association}}

formulas.name: Degree of Dissociation
formulas.latex: \alpha = \frac{i - 1}{n - 1} \qquad n = \text{number of ions produced per formula unit}

formulas.name: Degree of Association
formulas.latex: \alpha = \frac{1 - i}{1 - 1/n} \qquad n = \text{number of molecules associated to form a polymer}

chapters.name: Electrochemistry
keyPoints: Dry Cell (Leclanché): Anode: $\text{Zn} \to \text{Zn}^{2+} + 2e^-$; Cathode: $\text{MnO}_2 + \text{NH}_4^+ + e^- \to \text{MnO(OH)} + \text{NH}_3$; $E \approx 1.5\text{ V}$.

Mercury Cell: Anode: $\text{Zn(Hg)} + 2\text{OH}^- \to \text{ZnO} + \text{H}_2\text{O} + 2e^-$; Cathode: $\text{HgO} + \text{H}_2\text{O} + 2e^- \to \text{Hg} + 2\text{OH}^-$; Overall: $\text{Zn(Hg)} + \text{HgO} \to \text{ZnO} + \text{Hg}$; $E = 1.35\text{ V}$ (constant throughout life as no net ionic concentration change occurs).

Lead Storage Battery (Discharging): Anode: $\text{Pb}(s) + \text{SO}_4^{2-} \to \text{PbSO}_4(s) + 2e^-$; Cathode: $\text{PbO}_2(s) + \text{SO}_4^{2-} + 4\text{H}^+ + 2e^- \to \text{PbSO}_4(s) + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(l)$; Overall: $\text{Pb}(s) + \text{PbO}_2(s) + 2\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4(aq) \to 2\text{PbSO}_4(s) + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(l)$. Recharging: Reactions reverse; density of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ rises.

$\text{H}_2\text{-O}_2$ Fuel Cell: Anode: $2\text{H}_2 + 4\text{OH}^- \to 4\text{H}_2\text{O} + 4e^-$; Cathode: $\text{O}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} + 4e^- \to 4\text{OH}^-$; Overall: $2\text{H}_2 + \text{O}_2 \to 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$; Efficiency $\approx 70\%$.

Rusting of Iron (Electrochemical Mechanism): Anode: $2\text{Fe}(s) \to 2\text{Fe}^{2+} + 4e^-$ ($E^\circ = -0.44\text{ V}$); Cathode: $\text{O}_2(g) + 4\text{H}^+ + 4e^- \to 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(l)$ ($E^\circ = 1.23\text{ V}$); Overall: $2\text{Fe} + \text{O}_2 + 4\text{H}^+ \to 2\text{Fe}^{2+} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$ ($E_{\text{cell}}^\circ = 1.67\text{ V}$). Rust: $2\text{Fe}^{2+} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} + \frac{1}{2}\text{O}_2 \to \text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3 \cdot x\text{H}_2\text{O} + 4\text{H}^+$.

formulas.name: Standard Cell Potential
formulas.latex: E_{\text{cell}}^\circ = E_{\text{cathode}}^\circ - E_{\text{anode}}^\circ = E_R^\circ - E_L^\circ \qquad \text{Standard reduction potentials (IUPAC)}

formulas.name: Nernst Equation (Electrode)
formulas.latex: E_{(M^{n+}/M)} = E_{(M^{n+}/M)}^\circ - \frac{RT}{nF}\ln\frac{1}{[M^{n+}]} = E^\circ - \frac{0.0591}{n}\log\frac{1}{[M^{n+}]} \qquad \text{At } T = 298\text{ K}, F = 96487\text{ C mol}^{-1} \approx 96500\text{ C}

formulas.name: Nernst Equation (Cell Reaction)
formulas.latex: E_{\text{cell}} = E_{\text{cell}}^\circ - \frac{RT}{nF}\ln Q = E_{\text{cell}}^\circ - \frac{0.0591}{n}\log\frac{[\text{Products}]^c}{[\text{Reactants}]^a} \qquad \text{For } aA + bB \xrightarrow{ne^-} cC + dD; Q = \frac{[C]^c[D]^d}{[A]^a[B]^b}

formulas.name: Equilibrium Constant (Kc)
formulas.latex: \log K_c = \frac{n E_{\text{cell}}^\circ}{0.0591} \text{ (at 298 K)} \qquad \text{At equilibrium: } E_{\text{cell}} = 0 \implies E_{\text{cell}}^\circ = \frac{2.303 RT}{nF}\log K_c

formulas.name: Gibbs Energy of Cell Reaction
formulas.latex: \Delta_r G = -n F E_{\text{cell}},\; \Delta_r G^\circ = -n F E_{\text{cell}}^\circ = -2.303 RT\log K_c \qquad E_{\text{cell}} \text{ is intensive; } \Delta_r G \text{ is extensive}

formulas.name: Resistance & Resistivity
formulas.latex: R = \rho\frac{l}{A},\; G = \frac{1}{R} = \kappa\frac{A}{l} \qquad R \text{ in } \Omega, \rho \text{ in } \Omega\text{ m}, G \text{ in S } (\Omega^{-1}), \kappa \text{ in S m}^{-1} \text{ or S cm}^{-1}

formulas.name: Cell Constant (G*)
formulas.latex: G^* = \frac{l}{A} = R \kappa \qquad \text{Measured using standard KCl solutions}

formulas.name: Molar Conductivity
formulas.latex: \Lambda_m = \frac{\kappa}{c} = \frac{1000 \times \kappa\text{ (in S cm}^{-1}\text{)}}{M\text{ (in mol L}^{-1}\text{)}} \qquad \text{Unit: S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1} \text{ (}1\text{ S m}^2\text{ mol}^{-1} = 10^4\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}\text{)}

formulas.name: Debye-Hückel-Onsager Equation
formulas.latex: \Lambda_m = \Lambda_m^\circ - A\sqrt{c} \qquad \text{For strong electrolytes; } A = \text{constant}

formulas.name: Kohlrausch’s Law
formulas.latex: \Lambda_m^\circ = \nu_+ \lambda_+^\circ + \nu_- \lambda_-^\circ \qquad \text{Limiting molar conductivity at infinite dilution}

formulas.name: Degree of Dissociation
formulas.latex: \alpha = \frac{\Lambda_m}{\Lambda_m^\circ} \qquad \text{For weak electrolytes}

formulas.name: Dissociation Constant (Ka)
formulas.latex: K_a = \frac{c\alpha^2}{1 - \alpha} = \frac{c \Lambda_m^2}{\Lambda_m^\circ(\Lambda_m^\circ - \Lambda_m)} \qquad \text{Ostwald's dilution law}

formulas.name: Faraday’s 1st Law of Electrolysis
formulas.latex: w = z Q = z I t = \frac{E}{96500} I t = \frac{M}{n F} I t \qquad z = \text{electrochemical equivalent}, E = \text{equivalent weight}

formulas.name: Faraday’s 2nd Law of Electrolysis
formulas.latex: \frac{w_1}{w_2} = \frac{E_1}{E_2} \qquad \text{For cells connected in series}

chapters.name: Chemical Kinetics
keyDerivations: Zero Order Integrated Rate Law: $-\frac{d[R]}{dt} = k[R]^0 = k \implies \int_{[R]_0}^{[R]} d[R] = -k\int_0^t dt \implies [R] - [R]_0 = -kt \implies [R] = [R]_0 - kt$. At $t = t_{1/2}$, $[R] = [R]_0/2 \implies t_{1/2} = \frac{[R]_0}{2k}$.

First Order Integrated Rate Law: $-\frac{d[R]}{dt} = k[R] \implies \int_{[R]_0}^{[R]} \frac{d[R]}{[R]} = -k\int_0^t dt \implies \ln\frac{[R]}{[R]_0} = -kt \implies k = \frac{2.303}{t}\log\frac{[R]_0}{[R]}$. At $t = t_{1/2}$, $[R] = [R]_0/2 \implies t_{1/2} = \frac{\ln 2}{k} = \frac{0.693}{k}$.

Gas Phase First Order Reaction ($A(g) \to B(g) + C(g)$): At $t=0$, $p_A = p_i$, $p_B = 0$, $p_C = 0$. At time $t$, $p_A = p_i - x$, $p_B = x$, $p_C = x$. Total pressure $p_t = p_i - x + x + x = p_i + x \implies x = p_t - p_i \implies p_A = p_i - (p_t - p_i) = 2p_i - p_t$. $k = \frac{2.303}{t}\log\frac{p_i}{p_A} = \frac{2.303}{t}\log\frac{p_i}{2p_i - p_t}$

formulas.name: Rate of Reaction
formulas.latex: r_{\text{avg}} = -\frac{1}{a}\frac{\Delta[A]}{\Delta t} = \frac{1}{c}\frac{\Delta[C]}{\Delta t},\; r_{\text{inst}} = -\frac{1}{a}\frac{d[A]}{dt} \qquad \text{For reaction: } aA + bB \to cC + dD

formulas.name: Rate Law & Order
formulas.latex: \text{Rate} = k[A]^x[B]^y,\; \text{Order } n = x + y \qquad x, y \text{ are experimentally determined powers}

formulas.name: Units of Rate Constant (k)
formulas.latex: \text{Units of } k = (\text{mol L}^{-1})^{1-n} \text{ s}^{-1} \qquad n = \text{order of reaction}

formulas.name: Zero Order Integrated Rate Law
formulas.latex: [R] = [R]_0 - kt \implies k = \frac{[R]_0 - [R]}{t} \qquad \text{Linear plot: } [R] \text{ vs } t \text{ (slope = } -k, \text{ intercept = } [R]_0\text{)}

formulas.name: Zero Order Half-Life
formulas.latex: t_{1/2} = \frac{[R]_0}{2k} \qquad t_{1/2} \propto [R]_0

formulas.name: First Order Integrated Rate Law
formulas.latex: [R] = [R]_0 e^{-kt} \implies k = \frac{2.303}{t}\log\frac{[R]_0}{[R]} \qquad \text{Linear plot: } \ln[R] \text{ vs } t \text{ (slope = } -k\text{) or } \log\frac{[R]_0}{[R]} \text{ vs } t \text{ (slope = } k/2.303\text{)}

formulas.name: First Order Half-Life
formulas.latex: t_{1/2} = \frac{\ln 2}{k} = \frac{0.693}{k} \qquad \text{Independent of initial concentration } [R]_0

formulas.name: First Order Gas Phase Reaction
formulas.latex: k = \frac{2.303}{t}\log\frac{p_i}{2p_i - p_t} \qquad \text{For } A(g) \to B(g) + C(g); p_i = \text{initial pressure}, p_t = \text{total pressure}

formulas.name: Arrhenius Equation
formulas.latex: k = A e^{-E_a/RT} \qquad A = \text{frequency factor}, E_a = \text{activation energy}

formulas.name: Logarithmic Arrhenius Forms
formulas.latex: \ln k = \ln A - \frac{E_a}{RT},\; \log k = \log A - \frac{E_a}{2.303 RT} \qquad \text{Plot of } \log k \text{ vs } 1/T \text{ has slope } = -\frac{E_a}{2.303 R}

formulas.name: Two-Temperature Arrhenius Form
formulas.latex: \log\frac{k_2}{k_1} = \frac{E_a}{2.303 R}\left[\frac{T_2 - T_1}{T_1 T_2}\right] \qquad k_1, k_2 \text{ are rate constants at } T_1, T_2

formulas.name: Collision Theory Rate
formulas.latex: \text{Rate} = P Z_{AB} e^{-E_a/RT} \qquad P = \text{steric factor}, Z_{AB} = \text{collision frequency}

chapters.name: The d- and f-Block Elements
keyPoints: Lanthanoid Contraction: The steady decrease in atomic and ionic radii along the lanthanoid series ($\text{La}^{3+} \to \text{Lu}^{3+}$) due to poor shielding of nuclear charge by $4f$ electrons. Consequence: Almost identical atomic radii for $4d$ and $5d$ pairs (e.g., $\text{Zr} = 160\text{ pm}$ and $\text{Hf} = 159\text{ pm}$), making their separation difficult.
Actinoid Contraction: Greater from element to element than lanthanoid contraction due to poorer shielding by $5f$ electrons.

Preparation of $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$: $4\text{FeCr}_2\text{O}_4 + 8\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 + 7\text{O}_2 \to 8\text{Na}_2\text{CrO}_4\text{ (yellow)} + 2\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3 + 8\text{CO}_2$; $2\text{Na}_2\text{CrO}_4 + 2\text{H}^+ \to \text{Na}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7\text{ (orange)} + 2\text{Na}^+ + \text{H}_2\text{O}$; $\text{Na}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7 + 2\text{KCl} \to \text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7\text{ (crystallises)} + 2\text{NaCl}$

Preparation of $\text{KMnO}_4$: $2\text{MnO}_2 + 4\text{KOH} + \text{O}_2 \to 2\text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4\text{ (dark green)} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$; $3\text{MnO}_4^{2-} + 4\text{H}^+ \to 2\text{MnO}_4^-\text{ (purple)} + \text{MnO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$ (or via electrolytic oxidation)

formulas.name: General Configuration (d-block)
formulas.latex: (n-1)d^{1-10} ns^{1-2} \qquad \text{Anomalous: Cr: } 3d^5 4s^1, \text{ Cu: } 3d^{10} 4s^1, \text{ Pd: } 4d^{10} 5s^0

formulas.name: General Configuration (f-block)
formulas.latex: (n-2)f^{1-14} (n-1)d^{0-1} ns^2 \qquad \text{Lanthanoids: } [\text{Xe}] 4f^{1-14} 5d^{0-1} 6s^2; \text{ Actinoids: } [\text{Rn}] 5f^{1-14} 6d^{0-1} 7s^2

formulas.name: Spin-Only Magnetic Moment
formulas.latex: \mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)}\text{ BM} \qquad n = \text{number of unpaired electrons}, 1\text{ BM} = \frac{eh}{4\pi m_e}

formulas.name: Chromate-Dichromate Equilibrium
formulas.latex: 2\text{CrO}_4^{2-} + 2\text{H}^+ \rightleftharpoons \text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \qquad \text{Yellow (alkaline/neutral)} \rightleftharpoons \text{Orange (acidic)}

formulas.name: Dichromate Half-Reaction
formulas.latex: \text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} + 14\text{H}^+ + 6e^- \to 2\text{Cr}^{3+} + 7\text{H}_2\text{O} \qquad E^\circ = +1.33\text{ V}

formulas.name: Permanganate Half-Reaction (Acidic)
formulas.latex: \text{MnO}_4^- + 8\text{H}^+ + 5e^- \to \text{Mn}^{2+} + 4\text{H}_2\text{O} \qquad E^\circ = +1.52\text{ V}

formulas.name: Permanganate Half-Reaction (Neutral/Alkaline)
formulas.latex: \text{MnO}_4^- + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} + 3e^- \to \text{MnO}_2 + 4\text{OH}^- \qquad E^\circ = +1.69\text{ V} \text{ (Oxidises I}^- \to \text{IO}_3^-, \text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-} \to \text{SO}_4^{2-}\text{)}

chapters.name: Coordination Compounds
keyPoints: Spectrochemical Series: $\text{I}^- < \text{Br}^- < \text{SCN}^- < \text{Cl}^- < \text{S}^{2-} < \text{F}^- < \text{OH}^- < \text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-} < \text{H}_2\text{O} < \text{NCS}^- < \text{edta}^{4-} < \text{NH}_3 < \text{en} < \text{CN}^- < \text{CO}$
Werner’s Theory: Primary valence is ionisable and corresponds to the oxidation state; secondary valence is non-ionisable, corresponds to the coordination number, and dictates spatial geometry.
Structural Isomerism: Linkage (ambidentate ligands), Coordination (interchange between spheres), Ionisation (counter ion swaps with ligand), Solvate/Hydrate.
Stereoisomerism: Geometrical (Cis/Trans, fac/mer), Optical (non-superimposable chiral entities like $[\text{Co(en)}_3]^{3+}$).

Synergic Bonding in Metal Carbonyls: $\sigma$-bond formed by donation of lone pair from carbonyl carbon into vacant metal orbital; $\pi$-backbond formed by back-donation from filled metal $d$-orbital into empty $\pi^*$ antibonding orbital of CO.

formulas.name: Octahedral CFSE
formulas.latex: \text{CFSE} = \left(-0.4 n_{t_{2g}} + 0.6 n_{e_g}\right)\Delta_o + mP \qquad n_{t_{2g}}, n_{e_g} = \text{electrons in } t_{2g}, e_g; P = \text{pairing energy}

formulas.name: Tetrahedral Splitting
formulas.latex: \Delta_t = \frac{4}{9}\Delta_o \qquad \text{Tetrahedral complexes are always high spin (} \Delta_t < P \text{)}

formulas.name: Magnetic Moment
formulas.latex: \mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)}\text{ BM} \qquad \text{Unpaired electrons } n \text{ determined via VBT / CFT}

formulas.name: Stability Constant
formulas.latex: \beta_n = K_1 \times K_2 \times \dots \times K_n \qquad \text{Overall stability constant of complex } [ML_n]

chapters.name: Haloalkanes and Haloarenes
keyPoints: Haloarenes are extremely unreactive towards nucleophilic substitution due to: Partial double bond character of C-Cl bond through resonance, $sp^2$ hybridised carbon holding electrons more tightly than $sp^3$, instability of phenyl cation, electrostatic repulsion between electron-rich arene ring and incoming nucleophile.

formulas.name: Darzen’s Process
formulas.latex: \text{R-OH} + \text{SOCl}_2 \to \text{R-Cl} + \text{SO}_2(g) \uparrow + \text{HCl}(g) \uparrow \qquad \text{Best method for pure alkyl chlorides}

formulas.name: Finkelstein Reaction
formulas.latex: \text{R-X} + \text{NaI} \xrightarrow{\text{dry acetone}} \text{R-I} + \text{NaX} \downarrow \qquad \text{X = Cl, Br; NaX precipitates out}

formulas.name: Swarts Reaction
formulas.latex: \text{R-Br} + \text{AgF} \to \text{R-F} + \text{AgBr} \qquad \text{Metal fluorides: AgF, Hg}_2\text{F}_2\text{, CoF}_2\text{, SbF}_3

formulas.name: Sandmeyer Reaction
formulas.latex: \text{Ar-N}_2^+\text{X}^- \xrightarrow{\text{Cu}_2\text{Cl}_2/\text{HCl}} \text{Ar-Cl} + \text{N}_2 \qquad \text{For introducing -Cl, -Br, -CN}

formulas.name: Gattermann Reaction
formulas.latex: \text{Ar-N}_2^+\text{X}^- \xrightarrow{\text{Cu}/\text{HCl}} \text{Ar-Cl} + \text{N}_2 + \text{CuX} \qquad \text{Lower yield than Sandmeyer}

formulas.name: SN2 Mechanism
formulas.latex: \text{Nu}^- + \text{R-X} \to [\text{Nu}\cdots\text{C}\cdots\text{X}]^{\ddagger} \to \text{Nu-R} + \text{X}^- \qquad \text{1-step, bimolecular, inversion, Reactivity: } 1^\circ > 2^\circ > 3^\circ

formulas.name: SN1 Mechanism
formulas.latex: \text{R-X} \xrightarrow{\text{slow}} \text{R}^+ + \text{X}^- \xrightarrow[\text{fast}]{\text{Nu}^-} \text{R-Nu} \qquad \text{2-step via planar carbocation, racemisation, Reactivity: } 3^\circ > 2^\circ > 1^\circ

formulas.name: Saytzeff’s Elimination
formulas.latex: \text{R-CH}_2\text{-CH(X)-R}' \xrightarrow{\text{alc. KOH}, \Delta} \text{R-CH=CH-R}' \qquad \text{More substituted alkene is major product}

formulas.name: Grignard Formation
formulas.latex: \text{R-X} + \text{Mg} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \text{R-MgX} \qquad \text{RMgX} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \to \text{R-H} + \text{Mg(OH)X}

formulas.name: Wurtz Reaction
formulas.latex: 2\text{R-X} + 2\text{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \text{R-R} + 2\text{NaX} \qquad \text{Symmetric alkanes}

formulas.name: Wurtz-Fittig Reaction
formulas.latex: \text{Ar-X} + \text{R-X} + 2\text{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \text{Ar-R} + 2\text{NaX} \qquad \text{Alkylarene formation}

formulas.name: Fittig Reaction
formulas.latex: 2\text{Ar-X} + 2\text{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \text{Ar-Ar} + 2\text{NaX} \qquad \text{Diphenyl formation}

formulas.name: Dow’s Process
formulas.latex: \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{Cl} \xrightarrow[623\text{ K},\; 300\text{ atm}]{(i)\text{ NaOH}} \xrightarrow{(ii)\text{ H}^+} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{OH} \qquad \text{Activated by -NO}_2 \text{ groups at o, p-positions}

formulas.name: Acid-Catalysed Hydration
formulas.latex: \text{R-CH=CH}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{H}^+} \text{R-CH(OH)-CH}_3 \qquad \text{Markovnikov addition (via carbocation)}

formulas.name: Hydroboration-Oxidation
formulas.latex: 6\text{R-CH=CH}_2 + \text{B}_2\text{H}_6 \to 2(\text{R-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2)_3\text{B} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_2\text{O}_2/\text{OH}^-} 3\text{R-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{OH} \qquad \text{Net Anti-Markovnikov addition of H}_2\text{O}

formulas.name: Grignard with Carbonyls
formulas.latex: \text{HCHO} + \text{RMgX} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+} 1^\circ\text{ Alcohol},\quad \text{R}'\text{CHO} + \text{RMgX} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+} 2^\circ\text{ Alcohol},\quad \text{R}'\text{COR}'' + \text{RMgX} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+} 3^\circ\text{ Alcohol}

formulas.name: Cumene Process for Phenol
formulas.latex: \text{Cumene} \xrightarrow{\text{O}_2} \text{Cumene Hydroperoxide} \xrightarrow{\text{H}^+/\text{H}_2\text{O}} \text{Phenol} + \text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3 \qquad \text{Industrial synthesis; acetone is valuable by-product}

formulas.name: Lucas Test
formulas.latex: \text{R-OH} + \text{conc. HCl} \xrightarrow{\text{anh. ZnCl}_2} \text{R-Cl} \downarrow + \text{H}_2\text{O} \qquad 3^\circ\text{: Immediate turbidity; } 2^\circ\text{: 5 min; } 1^\circ\text{: No turbidity at room temp}

formulas.name: Dehydration of Alcohols
formulas.latex: \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \xrightarrow[443\text{ K}]{\text{conc. H}_2\text{SO}_4} \text{CH}_2\text{=CH}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O},\quad 2\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \xrightarrow[413\text{ K}]{\text{conc. H}_2\text{SO}_4} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{-O-CH}_2\text{CH}_3 \qquad \text{Ease: } 3^\circ > 2^\circ > 1^\circ

formulas.name: Kolbe’s Reaction
formulas.latex: \text{Phenol} \xrightarrow{\text{NaOH}} \text{Sodium Phenoxide} \xrightarrow[(ii)\text{ H}^+]{(i)\text{ CO}_2,\; \Delta} \text{Salicylic acid} \qquad \text{Electrophilic substitution by weak electrophile CO}_2

formulas.name: Reimer-Tiemann Reaction
formulas.latex: \text{Phenol} + \text{CHCl}_3 + 3\text{NaOH} \xrightarrow{\text{H}^+} \text{Salicylaldehyde} \qquad \text{Intermediate is dichlorocarbene (}:\text{CCl}_2\text{)}

formulas.name: Reaction with Zinc Dust
formulas.latex: \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{OH} + \text{Zn} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{C}_6\text{H}_6 + \text{ZnO} \qquad \text{Deoxygenation of phenol to benzene}

formulas.name: Williamson Ether Synthesis
formulas.latex: \text{R-X} + \text{R}'\text{ONa} \to \text{R-O-R}' + \text{NaX} \qquad \text{R-X must be } 1^\circ\text{; } 3^\circ\text{ R-X gives alkene exclusively}

formulas.name: Cleavage of Ethers by HI
formulas.latex: \text{R-O-R}' + \text{HI} \to \text{R-I} + \text{R}'\text{OH} \text{ (for } 1^\circ/2^\circ \text{ alkyls via S}_{N}2\text{)},\quad \text{tert-Butyl-O-CH}_3 + \text{HI} \to \text{tert-Butyl-I} + \text{CH}_3\text{OH} \text{ (via S}_{N}1\text{)} \qquad \text{Anisole gives Phenol + CH}_3\text{I}

chapters.name: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids
keyPoints: Relative Acidity Order of Carboxylic Acids: $\text{CF}_3\text{COOH} > \text{CCl}_3\text{COOH} > \text{CHCl}_2\text{COOH} > \text{NO}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH} > \text{NC-CH}_2\text{COOH} > \text{FCH}_2\text{COOH} > \text{ClCH}_2\text{COOH} > \text{BrCH}_2\text{COOH} > \text{HCOOH} > \text{ClCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH} > \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COOH} > \text{CH}_3\text{COOH} > \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$

formulas.name: Rosenmund Reduction
formulas.latex: \text{RCOCl} + \text{H}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Pd/BaSO}_4} \text{RCHO} + \text{HCl} \qquad \text{Poisoned catalyst prevents further reduction to alcohol}

formulas.name: Stephen Reaction
formulas.latex: \text{R-CN} + \text{SnCl}_2 + \text{HCl} \to \text{R-CH=NH} \cdot \text{HCl} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+} \text{RCHO} \qquad \text{Reduction of nitriles to aldehydes}

formulas.name: DIBAL-H Reduction
formulas.latex: \text{R-CN} \text{ or } \text{R-COOR}' \xrightarrow[(ii)\text{ H}_2\text{O}]{(i)\text{ DIBAL-H}} \text{RCHO} \qquad \text{Selective reduction at low temperature}

formulas.name: Étard Reaction
formulas.latex: \text{Toluene} + \text{CrO}_2\text{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{CS}_2} \text{Cr-complex} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+} \text{Benzaldehyde} \qquad \text{Selective methyl oxidation}

formulas.name: Gattermann-Koch Reaction
formulas.latex: \text{Benzene} + \text{CO} + \text{HCl} \xrightarrow{\text{anh. AlCl}_3/\text{CuCl}} \text{Benzaldehyde} \qquad \text{Formylation of benzene}

formulas.name: Clemmensen Reduction
formulas.latex: >\text{C=O} \xrightarrow{\text{Zn-Hg / conc. HCl}} >\text{CH}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \qquad \text{Reduction of carbonyl to methylene in acidic medium}

formulas.name: Wolff-Kishner Reduction
formulas.latex: >\text{C=O} \xrightarrow{\text{NH}_2\text{NH}_2, -\text{H}_2\text{O}} >\text{C=NNH}_2 \xrightarrow[\Delta]{\text{KOH / ethylene glycol}} >\text{CH}_2 + \text{N}_2 \qquad \text{Reduction in basic medium}

formulas.name: Tollens’ Test
formulas.latex: \text{RCHO} + 2[\text{Ag(NH}_3)_2]^+ + 3\text{OH}^- \to \text{RCOO}^- + 2\text{Ag} \downarrow\text{ (mirror)} + 4\text{NH}_3 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \qquad \text{Distinguishes aldehydes from ketones}

formulas.name: Fehling’s Test
formulas.latex: \text{RCHO} + 2\text{Cu}^{2+} + 5\text{OH}^- \to \text{RCOO}^- + \text{Cu}_2\text{O} \downarrow\text{ (red-brown)} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O} \qquad \text{Aromatic aldehydes do not respond}

formulas.name: Haloform (Iodoform) Test
formulas.latex: \text{R-CO-CH}_3 + 3\text{NaOI} \to \text{R-COONa} + \text{CHI}_3 \downarrow\text{ (yellow)} + 2\text{NaOH} \qquad \text{Specific for CH}_3\text{C=O and CH}_3\text{CH(OH)- groups}

formulas.name: Aldol Condensation
formulas.latex: 2\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} \xrightarrow{\text{dil. NaOH}} \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CHO} \xrightarrow[\Delta]{-\text{H}_2\text{O}} \text{CH}_3\text{CH=CH-CHO} \qquad \text{Requires at least one } \alpha\text{-H}

formulas.name: Cannizzaro Reaction
formulas.latex: 2\text{HCHO} \xrightarrow{\text{conc. KOH}} \text{CH}_3\text{OH} + \text{HCOOK} \qquad \text{Disproportionation of aldehydes lacking } \alpha\text{-H}

formulas.name: Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky (HVZ)
formulas.latex: \text{R-CH}_2\text{-COOH} \xrightarrow[(ii)\text{ H}_2\text{O}]{(i)\text{ X}_2/\text{red P}} \text{R-CH(X)-COOH} \qquad \text{X = Cl, Br; halogenation at } \alpha\text{-carbon}

formulas.name: Decarboxylation
formulas.latex: \text{R-COONa} + \text{NaOH} \xrightarrow[\Delta]{\text{CaO}} \text{R-H} + \text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 \qquad \text{Sodalime ratio is 3:1}

chapters.name: Amines
keyPoints: Basicity Trends in Amines: Gaseous Phase: $3^\circ > 2^\circ > 1^\circ > \text{NH}_3$ (governed solely by +I inductive effect).

Aqueous Phase (Ethyl-substituted): $(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5)_2\text{NH} > (\text{C}_2\text{H}_5)_3\text{N} > \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2 > \text{NH}_3$ ($2^\circ > 3^\circ > 1^\circ > \text{NH}_3$).
Aqueous Phase (Methyl-substituted): $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{NH} > \text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2 > (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{N} > \text{NH}_3$ ($2^\circ > 1^\circ > 3^\circ > \text{NH}_3$).
Aromatic Amines: Aniline is weaker than ammonia ($pK_b = 9.38$ vs $4.75$) due to resonance delocalisation of the nitrogen lone pair into the ring.

formulas.name: Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis
formulas.latex: \text{Phthalimide} \xrightarrow{\text{KOH}} \text{Potassium Phthalimide} \xrightarrow{\text{R-X}} \text{N-Alkylphthalimide} \xrightarrow{\text{NaOH}(aq)} 1^\circ\text{ Amine} + \text{Sodium Phthalate} \qquad \text{Pure } 1^\circ \text{ aliphatic amines only}

formulas.name: Hoffmann Bromamide Degradation
formulas.latex: \text{R-CONH}_2 + \text{Br}_2 + 4\text{NaOH} \to \text{R-NH}_2 + \text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 + 2\text{NaBr} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \qquad \text{Product has one less carbon than starting amide}

formulas.name: Carbylamine Test
formulas.latex: \text{R-NH}_2 + \text{CHCl}_3 + 3\text{KOH} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{R-NC}\text{ (isocyanide)} + 3\text{KCl} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O} \qquad \text{Specific test for } 1^\circ \text{ aliphatic and aromatic amines}

formulas.name: Hinsberg’s Test
formulas.latex: 1^\circ\text{ Amine} + \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{SO}_2\text{Cl} \to \text{Soluble in alkali}; \quad 2^\circ\text{ Amine} + \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{SO}_2\text{Cl} \to \text{Insoluble in alkali}; \quad 3^\circ\text{ Amine} + \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{SO}_2\text{Cl} \to \text{No Reaction} \qquad \text{Reagent: Benzenesulphonyl chloride}

formulas.name: Diazotisation
formulas.latex: \text{Ar-NH}_2 + \text{NaNO}_2 + 2\text{HCl} \xrightarrow{273-278\text{ K}} \text{Ar-N}_2^+\text{Cl}^- + \text{NaCl} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \qquad \text{Low temperature required to prevent decomposition}

formulas.name: Azo Coupling (with Phenol)
formulas.latex: \text{Ar-N}_2^+\text{Cl}^- + \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{OH} \xrightarrow{\text{OH}^-,\; \text{pH } 9-10} \text{p-hydroxyazobenzene} + \text{Cl}^- + \text{H}_2\text{O} \qquad \text{Orange dye}

formulas.name: Azo Coupling (with Aniline)
formulas.latex: \text{Ar-N}_2^+\text{Cl}^- + \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{H}^+,\; \text{pH } 4-5} \text{p-aminoazobenzene} + \text{Cl}^- + \text{H}_2\text{O} \qquad \text{Yellow dye}

chapters.name: Biomolecules
keyPoints: D-(+)-Glucose: Aldohexose (6-carbon polyhydroxy aldehyde); Pyranose ring ($\alpha$ and $\beta$ anomers at C1).
D-(-)-Fructose: Ketohexose; Furanose ring ($\alpha$ and $\beta$ anomers at C2). Laevorotatory, sweetest naturally occurring sugar.
Sucrose: $\alpha$-D-Glucopyranose (C1) + $\beta$-D-Fructofuranose (C2); Glycosidic linkage. Non-reducing sugar; hydrolyses to give Invert Sugar (dextro $\to$ laevo).
Maltose: $\alpha$-D-Glucose (C1) + $\alpha$-D-Glucose (C4). Reducing sugar (free aldehyde at C1 of 2nd glucose).
Lactose: $\beta$-D-Galactose (C1) + $\beta$-D-Glucose (C4). Milk sugar; reducing sugar.
Starch: Amylose (15–20%, unbranched, $\alpha$-1,4-linkage) + Amylopectin (80–85%, branched, $\alpha$-1,4-chain with $\alpha$-1,6-branches). Storage polysaccharide in plants.
Cellulose: Linear polymer of $\beta$-D-Glucose ($\beta$-1,4-glycosidic linkage). Chief constituent of plant cell walls.

Amino Acids: Contain -$\text{NH}_2$ and -$\text{COOH}$; exist as Zwitterion ($\text{H}_3\text{N}^+-\text{CHR}-\text{COO}^-$). All natural $\alpha$-amino acids have L-configuration; Glycine is achiral.

Proteins: Polymers of $\alpha$-amino acids joined by Peptide bonds (-$\text{CO}-\text{NH}$-). Primary: Amino acid sequence; Secondary: $\alpha$-Helix & $\beta$-Pleated sheet (H-bonding); Tertiary: Overall folding; Quaternary: Assembly of polypeptide subunits.
Denaturation: Uncoiling of helix and loss of biological activity. Disrupts $2^\circ$ and $3^\circ$ structures; $1^\circ$ structure remains intact.

Nucleic Acids: Polynucleotides connected via 3', 5'-phosphodiester linkages. DNA: $\beta$-D-2-deoxyribose + A, G, C, T (Double stranded). RNA: $\beta$-D-ribose + A, G, C, U (Single stranded). Base Pairing: Adenine = Thymine (2 H-bonds); Guanine $\equiv$ Cytosine (3 H-bonds).
Fat-Soluble Vitamins (A, D, E, K): A (Xerophthalmia, Night blindness), D (Rickets, Osteomalacia), E (Increased RBC fragility), K (Increased blood clotting time).
Water-Soluble Vitamins (B-complex, C): $\text{B}_1$ (Beri-beri), $\text{B}_2$ (Cheilosis), $\text{B}_6$ (Convulsions), $\text{B}_{12}$ (Pernicious anaemia), C (Scurvy).

formulas.name: Glucose Reactions 1
formulas.latex: \text{Glucose} \xrightarrow{\text{HI}, \Delta} \text{n-hexane}

formulas.name: Glucose Reactions 2
formulas.latex: \text{Glucose} \xrightarrow{\text{Br}_2/\text{H}_2\text{O}} \text{Gluconic acid}

formulas.name: Glucose Reactions 3
formulas.latex: \text{Glucose} \xrightarrow{\text{conc. HNO}_3} \text{Saccharic acid}
